prompt:
Use the attached clay render as the exact blueprint. Keep every wall, opening, window, cornice, skirting, floor and ceiling line, the camera height, lens and angle, and the position, size and angle of every furniture piece and built-in exactly as in the clay. Move, resize, add or remove nothing. Each placeholder shape in the clay marks one product listed below; render it there at the stated size. Only turn the clay into real materials and light. The other attached images are close-ups of the exact products: match their form, colour and texture. Positions are fractions of frame width (x) and height (y) from the top-left.

1. PHOTO. A frame from a camera move through the same house: the same room, products, light and grade as the attached master photograph (reference 1), which is taken from another camera; the clay alone sets the framing, the position and the size of everything; render only what this clay shows. 24 mm shift lens at 1.1 m, level, straight verticals, all sharp.

2. LIGHT. One key: soft daylight from the east window at the left edge, no sun; outside, bare birches, no snow, no buildings. Exposed for white: the wall beside the window clean white, a step under the glowing reveal; the glass brightest, detailed. Light rakes left to right and falls off half a stop toward the kitchen's far end. Every piece: a lit window face, a shadow side a stop darker; table, chairs and bench cast long soft shadows right and toward the camera; dense contact shadows. Ceiling a touch darker, darkest top right. Real contrast, never milky. 4600 K: whites white, never cream, pink or grey. Lamps 2700 K, low, shadowless: the lantern glows from within and lays a warm pool on the table top, the warmest wood in the frame; hidden LED strips under both shelves wash the upstand in soft gradients.

3. MATERIALS. Matte mineral paint #F4F1EC. Wide oiled white-oak planks, pale honey #D6BF9E. Table, chairs, bench, shelves: oiled oak #C8A27A, satin sheen, a long soft window highlight along the table top. Kitchen: flat handleless warm-white matte fronts, honed light limestone counter and upstand, matte black tap; the hood in warm-white lime plaster, its trowelled texture caught by the raking light.

4. PRODUCTS, one per line, each on its clay placeholder:
a. LANTERN, x 0.52-0.63, y 0.00-0.30: a flat ribbed warm-white silk pumpkin lantern, 50 wide, thin black rod, bottom 75 cm above the table.
b. RUNNER along the table axis, x 0.41-0.71, y 0.58-0.64: stone-washed oat linen 40 x 140, soft crumple, plain hem.
c. VASE on the runner under the lantern, x 0.54-0.61, y 0.41-0.61: 26 cm warm-white matte stoneware, 3-5 olive sprigs.
d. CANDLE PLATES left of it, x 0.47-0.54, y 0.53-0.62: two palm-sized matte black iron plates, unlit pillar candles 15 and 10 cm.
e. CURTAIN, x 0.43-0.47, y 0.00-0.75: one sheer natural linen-blend panel, narrow S-fold stack, slim black rod, backlit, hem on the floor.
f. BENCH PAD, x 0.55-0.88, y 0.73-0.91: off-white linen-look cushion, 3 cm thin, the full bench length.
g. RUG under table and chairs, x 0.24-0.97, y 0.74-1.00: flat hand-woven off-white wool, visible loom slub.
h. PRINT on the left shelf, x 0.78-0.83, y 0.25-0.35: 30 x 40, taupe block and black line on white, thin black frame, leaning; nothing else on that shelf.
m. KITCHEN RUNNER before the counter, x 0.67-1.00, y 0.73-0.92: 60 x 280 ivory wool, low pile, thin line border.

5. NOT IN FRAME: floor vase, wall lamp, sink set, utensil jar, boards, plants, other food, appliances, books, glass, text, people. No sun patches, beams, bloom, haze, halos, HDR, grain or vignette.
prompt_deviation: lines starting with # stripped as the header instructs

grade.rule: docs/render-recipe-nordic-2026-10-24.md 2.6 (the Bible grade): WB on the hero-wall patch, exposure capped +-0.2 stop, chroma -10%, roll-off from L 94, S curve 0.12, black point to L 12.5 only if below 12, no grain, no vignette

overscan.note: same camera and focal length in pixels; the 16:9 frame is the centre crop; uv in this selfcheck (boxes, patches) are fractions of the canvas
overscan.motion_agent: -graded-os6.png = the 16:9 frame plus 0.0303 of its height above and below (--a-overscan / --b-overscan)

clay_lock.method: regions = whole frame, quadrants, ceiling/floor bands and the clay boxes of fixed furniture / windows / openings; peaks below ~0.03 are unreliable (weak texture), so the verdict is visual (<aid>-lock.png) with the strong-peak number as support

verdict.visual: HELD: window, walls, table, chairs, bench, lantern, shelf and kitchen run on the clay lines

product_check.rule: each product inside its clay box +-15 % of the box size (<aid>-boxes.png); read visually
